solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Heavenly pair of legs exposed after pulling back short skirt (6)

indicatorNotes.exposed: a word exposed has its outer covering stripped away
indicatorNotes.pulling back: pulled back, the letters run the other way

blocks.note: LEGS without its outer letters; then turned round to GE

annotation.surface: A leg-flashing moment as a short skirt is hitched back, with 'heavenly' as the admirer's verdict.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pair of legs' reads as a pair of limbs, but it is the two letters left when LEGS is exposed. 'Heavenly pair' is the twins of the zodiac.
annotation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is the constellation of Castor and Pollux, a pair in the heavens.

entries.clue: Household troops informed main source of protection? (9)

blocks.note: the Household Division's regiments are the Guards

annotation.surface: A question about which troops really keep the royal household safe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main, so a source of protection on the main is a ship on guard duty; the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A guardship is a warship stationed to protect a harbour or coast, so it protects at sea.

entries.clue: Corrupt pimp and waiter nearly do bird (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Corrupt: corrupted letters are spoilt and rearranged
indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly a word is the word short of its last letter

annotation.surface: A crooked pimp and a waiter conspiring to do someone in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do bird' reads as serve a prison sentence (bird is slang for jail time), but 'do' is fodder and 'bird' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The meadow pipit is a small brown songbird of open grassland.

entries.clue: In tours, deviating from N (7)

indicatorNotes.deviating: letters that deviate stray from their order

annotation.surface: A travel note about tours that stray from due north.
annotation.walkthrough: N reads as the compass point north, but it is the chemical symbol for nitrogen.
annotation.definitionFit: Nitrous means containing or derived from nitrogen, whose symbol is N.

entries.clue: Fungus still hides a stone design (5,5)

indicatorNotes.hides: one word hides the others by wrapping round them

annotation.surface: A fungus lurking in a carved stone pattern.
annotation.walkthrough: A stone is also a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST. YET opens to hold A, ST and PLAN.
annotation.definitionFit: Yeast is a single-celled fungus, and older botany filed fungi under plants, hence the name.

entries.clue: Spear carrier no longer part of mounted paintings? (5)

indicatorNotes.mounted: in a down answer, mounted letters climb upwards, so they read in reverse

annotation.surface: A question about a soldier's spear dropped from an exhibition of framed paintings.
annotation.walkthrough: A spear carrier is theatre slang for an actor with a walk-on part, someone who stands at the back holding a spear.
annotation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer with a minor non-speaking role, the classic spear carrier.

entries.clue: Endlessly cheated clients finally sink aged earl (11)

indicatorNotes.Endlessly: a word without end loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.finally: finally points to the last letter

annotation.surface: A swindler's victims getting their own back by doing away with an old aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: Shafted is slang for cheated. The Earls of Shaftesbury include the 7th Earl, the Victorian reformer who lived to 84.
annotation.definitionFit: Shaftesbury is an earldom, so an Earl of Shaftesbury, here an old one.

entries.clue: Brief spell standing is controlling tense twitch of membranous inflammation (11)

indicatorNotes.Brief: a brief word is cut short at the end
indicatorNotes.standing: in a down answer, standing letters rise upwards, so they read in reverse
indicatorNotes.controlling: to control is to hold within

blocks.note: T = tense, the grammar label; ITS then stands up to STI

annotation.surface: A medical note about a short bout of a membrane inflammation whose twitch is held in check.
annotation.walkthrough: IS holds T to make ITS, which reads upward as STI. The periosteum is the membrane that covers bone.
annotation.definitionFit: Periostitic describes periostitis, inflammation of the periosteum membrane.

entries.clue: Those who take on publicity edited poster (8)

annotation.surface: People who took on a publicity job and then reworked the poster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Publicity' and 'poster' belong together in the surface, but only one is fodder; the other just gives AD.
annotation.definitionFit: Adopters are those who take on a child, pet or idea as their own.

entries.clue: Abstemious relief over many years, note (9)

blocks.note: a temp is a stand-in, someone brought in as relief
an era = a long span of years
te = the seventh note of the scale

annotation.surface: Someone who took the pledge, feeling relieved after years on the wagon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Relief' reads as a feeling, but it is a person: a relief worker covering someone's shift, a temp.
annotation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate, especially in drinking, which is what abstemious means.

entries.clue: Infant, last to sulk, overturned dish (5)

indicatorNotes.last to: the last of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A sulking toddler throwing their dinner on the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: BABE then K makes BABEK, which read backwards is KEBAB. The surface's flipped dish is exactly what the wordplay does to the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A kebab is a dish of meat pieces cooked on a skewer.

entries.clue: Binding regularly stops vital organ (6)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a gap is to fill it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: key = vital, as in a key issue

annotation.surface: A contract that stops a vital organ from being used.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vital organ' looks like the whole definition, but 'vital' is KEY and only 'organ' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the blood-filtering bean-shaped body part is one of the body's organs.

entries.clue: Long veiled garment thus covering half of face when going around in African republic (7,4)

indicatorNotes.covering: in a down answer, a word covering another sits on top of it, so SO comes below FA
indicatorNotes.half of: half of a word keeps just its first half
indicatorNotes.going around: one word goes around another to hold it

blocks.note: the burka covers the body and face; it goes around IN

annotation.surface: A description of a veiled robe worn in an African country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In African republic' reads as where the garment is worn, but the 'in' is a letter pair to be wrapped. The burka is a full-body Muslim garment with a mesh over the face.
annotation.definitionFit: Burkina Faso is a landlocked republic in West Africa.

entries.clue: Elementary programming language (5)

blocks.note: an adjective: fundamental, at the simplest level
a 1960s computer language written for beginners

annotation.surface: A description of a beginners' computer language.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, an easy programming language, but each half defines the answer on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for elementary, and also the acronym-named language (Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code).

entries.clue: Supportive system reduced healthy food, say (7,5)

indicatorNotes.reduced: a reduced word is cut short

annotation.surface: A diet plan with smaller portions of healthy food as a support regime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' reads as 'for example', but here it is a verb meaning state.
annotation.definitionFit: The welfare state is the government system of benefits that supports citizens.

entries.clue: Not being taken into account, blokes start to trash flat (9)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Some men, ignored by everyone, beginning to wreck a flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Apart' as in 'joking apart': set aside and not taken into account. Blokes is British slang for men.
annotation.definitionFit: Flat is the British word and apartment the American one for the same set of rooms on one floor.

entries.clue: Ranks quality soldiers in places to go? (3,10)

indicatorNotes.in: soldiers in places means the soldiers sit inside the word for the places

blocks.note: an air = a quality or manner
commodes = chamber pots in chairs; they hold OR

annotation.surface: Soldiers of good quality ranked up in the places they are posted to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Places to go?' hints at loos, so commodes. 'Ranks' is the definition read as a plural noun: holders of a rank.
annotation.definitionFit: Air commodores are officers of a Royal Air Force rank, so ranks here stands for rank-holders.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Ranks' stands for the people holding that rank

entries.clue: Doctor on a trip after work’s decline (4,3)

indicatorNotes.after: after sends the trip's letters OFF to follow OP

blocks.note: op = opus, a work; OFF follows it

annotation.surface: A doctor whose trip after work coincides with some falling-off.
annotation.walkthrough: Op is the short form of opus, a musical work.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fall in numbers, as when sales tail away, is both a decline and a drop-off.

entries.clue: Uncovered rudimentary boats, nearly all nearest the stern (7)

indicatorNotes.Uncovered: an uncovered word loses its outer letters
indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly a word is the word short of its last letter

blocks.note: RAFTS with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: Open rafts, almost all of them lying at the back of the boat.
annotation.walkthrough: Rafts are the rudimentary boats, lashed-together logs. 'Nearly all' is a synonym (MOST), not a cutting instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Aftmost means furthest aft, the part of a ship nearest the stern.

entries.clue: Mournful stage of journey, one in unlimited silence (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'one in silence' places the stage and the one inside the silence
indicatorNotes.unlimited: an unlimited word has its outer letters removed

blocks.note: PEACE without its outer letters; it holds LEG and I

annotation.surface: A sad step of a journey, one made in total silence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silence' is PEACE (as in peace and quiet), and 'unlimited' strips its first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Elegiac means mournful, in the manner of an elegy.

entries.clue: I’m optimistic sleeping partners should move on shop’s contents (4,7,7)

indicatorNotes.should move: letters that move change their order
indicatorNotes.contents: a word's contents are its inside letters

annotation.surface: Business investors who never do anything being told to clear out the stock.
annotation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner is a business investor who takes no active part. The definition speaks in the first person: saying the proverb is how you declare you are hopeful.
annotation.definitionFit: Saying 'hope springs eternal' amounts to saying I'm optimistic.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a first-person statement, standing for the saying that expresses it

entries.clue: Recently discovered large dog misses country (3-5)

indicatorNotes.misses: a word that misses something leaves it out

blocks.note: the Newfoundland, a big breed of dog

annotation.surface: A huge dog pining for its homeland.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog is named after Newfoundland, an island, which makes 'country' look like a clue to the dog itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something found only newly, like new-found confidence, was recently discovered.

entries.clue: Dishonourable sort beginning to interrupt judge (4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a cad = a man who behaves dishonourably

annotation.surface: A bounder starting to heckle a judge in court.
annotation.walkthrough: Cad is an old British word for a man who behaves badly towards women.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadi, or qadi, is a judge in Islamic law.

entries.clue: Lives to embrace church, your one-time Christian emblem (7)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: to embrace is to hold inside

blocks.note: is = lives, exists; it goes around the rest

annotation.surface: A declaration that one lives embracing the church and the old symbol of Christianity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One-time' says the word is archaic: THY is the old your.
annotation.definitionFit: The ichthys is the fish symbol used by early Christians.

entries.clue: Work very hard, as shown by unaccompanied male you found in bar (4,1,3)

indicatorNotes.found in: these letters are found inside another word

blocks.note: but = except, bar; it holds STAG and U
going stag = a man going alone

annotation.surface: A lone man at the bar, sweating to get served.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a pub, but it is the preposition meaning except: BUT.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: straining so hard you might rupture your belly means working very hard.

entries.clue: Young pigeon quietly enters pillar (5)

indicatorNotes.enters: one word enters another, going inside

blocks.note: a pier = a supporting pillar; it takes in P

annotation.surface: A young pigeon slipping quietly into a column.
annotation.walkthrough: A pier in architecture is a solid support between arches, so a pillar.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary-only sense: a squab still cheeping, a piping chick, is called this.

entries.clue: Dropping announcement, radar on a destroyer raised unusual thing (4,4)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down answer, raised letters go upwards, so they read in reverse

blocks.note: an ad = an announcement; dropped from radar
Siva, or Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction; raised to AVIS

annotation.surface: A warship's radar raised on deck without any announcement, which is odd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' reads as a warship, but it is the Hindu god Siva, the destroyer of the trinity.
annotation.definitionFit: Rara avis, Latin for rare bird, means an unusual person or thing.

entries.clue: Understood Springfield’s concerned with remnants of deal? (8)

annotation.surface: Grasping what a pop singer was doing with leftovers from a business deal.
annotation.walkthrough: Deal is also pine or fir timber, so its remnants after sawing are sawdust. Dusty Springfield was a 1960s British pop singer.
annotation.definitionFit: Sawdusty means of or covered in sawdust, the leftovers of sawn wood.

entries.clue: Pass on development, saving outskirts in spa town (8)

indicatorNotes.saving outskirts: saving means except, so the word is taken without its outer letters
indicatorNotes.in: development in spa town places those letters inside the town

blocks.note: Bath, the English spa city; it holds EQUE

annotation.surface: Handing on a property development, but keeping the land on the edges of a spa town.
annotation.walkthrough: A sequel is a development, as in a later turn of events. 'Saving' means except here, not keeping.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: leaving your goods to heirs in a will is passing them on.

entries.clue: Past leader of Ireland, old success in House (8)

indicatorNotes.in: success in House puts the Irish, old and success letters inside the house

blocks.note: ho = house; it holds the rest

annotation.surface: A former Irish leader whose old success came in the House.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Past leader of Ireland' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'leader'; Ireland is only IR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Japan's wartime emperor, who died in 1989, is a leader of the past.

entries.clue: Acting to root out former right-winger about what’s behind covert Irish past, half-forgotten (11)

indicatorNotes.about: one word goes about the others, surrounding them
indicatorNotes.what’s behind: what is behind a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.half-forgotten: half of the word is left out

blocks.note: ex-Tory; it goes about the rest

annotation.surface: A purge of a one-time Conservative who hid a secret Irish past.
annotation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, so an ex-Tory is a former right-winger.
annotation.definitionFit: Extirpatory means serving to extirpate, to root out entirely.

entries.clue: Key party cutting American currency overseas (7)

indicatorNotes.cutting: a word cutting another goes into it

annotation.surface: A key political party slashing the American dollar's value abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as important, but it is a keyboard key: Esc.
annotation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal and is still used in Cape Verde.

entries.clue: Hi-tech tools damaged natural breaker? (6,5)

indicatorNotes.damaged: damaged letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: Expensive modern tools broken, with a question about what could do that naturally.
annotation.walkthrough: The contrast is the joke: machines break but a rodent carries its own cutter.
annotation.definitionFit: A chisel tooth is a rodent's incisor, a tool nature grew for gnawing and breaking things.

entries.clue: Specialist in instruction — journalist, one that’s positively charged in Hebridean islands (12)

indicatorNotes.in: the charged one in the islands sits inside the islands' name

blocks.note: North and South Uist, in the Outer Hebrides; it holds CATION
a cation = a positively charged ion

annotation.surface: A teacher, a reporter and a live wire all turning up on the Scottish isles.
annotation.walkthrough: Uist names two islands, North and South, which is why 'islands' is plural.
annotation.definitionFit: An educationist is an expert in the theory and methods of education.

entries.clue: Seaweed extract, free of iodine, bearing English granny (11)

indicatorNotes.free of: a word free of a letter has lost it

blocks.note: CARRIAGE (how one carries oneself) free of I

annotation.surface: A seaweed tonic with no iodine in it, carried by an English grandmother.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' reads as carrying, but it is the noun: carriage, the way someone holds themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: Carrageenan is a thickener extracted from red seaweed.

entries.clue: Renewal of interest earning weak spoils (11)

indicatorNotes.spoils: spoilt letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: A banker's lament that feeble interest earnings ruin everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interest' reads as bank interest, and 'earning' and 'spoils' keep that money story going, though the definition means curiosity.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: curiosity or feeling stirring again after lying dormant is a renewal of interest.

entries.clue: Italians in part tide over poor Latin society (11)

indicatorNotes.poor: poor letters are in bad shape, rearranged

annotation.surface: Some Italians coping with a tide over their poorer Latin neighbours.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In part' belongs to the definition: Neapolitans are Italians from one part of Italy. A neap tide is the small tide between springs.
annotation.definitionFit: Neapolitans are people from Naples, Italians from one part of the country.

entries.clue: Eccentric hurls corgis for those who might offer kicks (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Eccentric: eccentric letters are out of their usual order

annotation.surface: An odd person flinging the Queen's dogs at those likely to kick them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' reads as cruelty or thrills; it is the high kicks of a line of dancers.
annotation.definitionFit: Chorus girls dance in a line, famously doing high kicks.

entries.clue: Angry copper was once lying about tool (8,3)

indicatorNotes.lying about: lying about, the letters are turned round

blocks.note: Cu, the chemical symbol for copper
wast, the old form of 'were' (thou wast); turned round to TSAW

annotation.surface: A furious police officer who used to lie about a weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a police officer, but it is the metal's symbol, Cu. 'Once' marks WAST as an archaic word.
annotation.definitionFit: A crosscut saw is a tool for cutting wood across the grain.

entries.clue: Possibly square career soldier accepts time in prison (11)

indicatorNotes.accepts: to accept is to take inside
indicatorNotes.in: time in prison is literal: the time goes inside the prison

blocks.note: a regular is a full-time professional soldier; it accepts CTAN
the can = prison; it holds T

annotation.surface: A strait-laced soldier doing time in jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Square' reads as conventional, which suits a career soldier, but it is the shape. 'Possibly' says a square is one kind of rectangle.
annotation.definitionFit: A square is a rectangle with equal sides, so a square is rectangular.

entries.clue: My beloved that is absorbing every moment to begin with (6,2)

indicatorNotes.absorbing: to absorb is to take inside
indicatorNotes.to begin with: the words to begin with give their first letters

blocks.note: ie = id est, that is; it absorbs EM
first letters of every and moment

annotation.surface: A lover declaring they are absorbed from the very first moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My beloved' reads as a phrase, but 'My' is on its own the exclamation of surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: Dearie me and my! are both mild exclamations of surprise or dismay.

entries.clue: Procure post-match train for my fans after leaving loudly (5,4)

indicatorNotes.fans: to fan is to spread letters out in a new order

blocks.note: TRAIN FOR MY without F; anagram fodder, 9 letters
f = forte, loudly; leaves the fodder

annotation.surface: Laying on a train home for the supporters after a match, departing noisily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fans' reads as supporters, but it is the verb: spreading the letters out. 'Post-match' means after a marriage, not a football game.
annotation.definitionFit: To marry into money or a family is to acquire it through the match of marriage.

entries.clue: Preserve withdrawn 50 per cent of olives with roughly glazed earthenware (8)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: withdrawn letters are drawn back, so they read in reverse
indicatorNotes.50 per cent of: fifty per cent is a half, so take the first half of the word

blocks.note: jam = a fruit preserve; withdrawn to MAJ

annotation.surface: A deli order: jam taken off the shelf, half the olives, and a rustic glazed pot.
annotation.walkthrough: Circa, shortened to ca, is used before approximate dates.
annotation.definitionFit: Majolica is tin-glazed earthenware, originally Italian.

entries.clue: At last outwit smart walrus? (5)

indicatorNotes.At last: at last points to the last letter

annotation.surface: Finally getting the better of a clever walrus.
annotation.walkthrough: A walrus is a droopy style of moustache, and tache is British slang for a moustache; the question mark says walrus is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the walrus, thick and drooping like the animal's whiskers, is one style of moustache.
annotation.definitionNote: the definition is an example of the answer

entries.clue: Classical trio of eg French, Italian and Spanish guys on cycling team (9)

indicatorNotes.cycling: cycled letters move the first to the end

blocks.note: SIDE cycled, its S moved to the end

annotation.surface: Three European riders in a cycle race team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' reads as the sport, but it moves the first letter of SIDE to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The Eumenides, or Furies, were the three goddesses of vengeance in Greek myth.

entries.clue: Extremely vile arachnid almost catching a family of wasps etc (8)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: the extremes of a word are its outer letters
indicatorNotes.almost: almost a word is the word short of its last letter
indicatorNotes.catching: to catch is to hold inside

blocks.note: SPIDER without its last letter; it catches A

annotation.surface: A nasty spider nearly catching a wasp.
annotation.walkthrough: Spiders do catch wasps, so the surface is a nature scene; the answer is the wasps' scientific family name.
annotation.definitionFit: Vespidae is the family of social wasps, hornets and their relatives.

entries.clue: Heroin — kilo kept in sink (4)

indicatorNotes.kept in: one part is kept inside another

annotation.surface: A kilo of heroin hidden in the kitchen sink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sink' reads as the kitchen fitting, but it is the verb: sag.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: street users' word for the drug.

entries.clue: This offence reduced by heads of Glaswegian Boys’ Homes (8,6,4)

annotation.definition: This offence reduced by heads of Glaswegian Boys’ Homes

blocks.note: the surface offers a crime being lessened; the setter means the offence shortened to its initials

blocks.clueFragment: by heads of Glaswegian Boys’ Homes
blocks.note: the first letters G, B and H are exactly those initials

annotation.surface: A scandal about crimes committed in Scottish children's homes.
annotation.walkthrough: The heads are the first letters G, B and H, and GBH is how this British criminal offence is abbreviated. The wordplay gives the abbreviation, not the letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Grievous bodily harm is a serious assault offence in British law, commonly called GBH.

entries.clue: Get zany wild flower from Asia (7)

indicatorNotes.wild: wild letters run out of order

annotation.surface: An instruction to go crazy over an exotic wild flower from Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a flow-er, something that flows: a river. 'Wild flower' looks like one phrase but 'wild' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river, so it flows through Asia.

entries.clue: Belittle class in dictation? (6)

indicatorNotes.in dictation: dictated words are spoken, so the sound counts

annotation.surface: A pupil made to feel small during a dictation exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: Lesson and lessen sound the same; dictation fits a classroom, which hides the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: To lessen can mean to belittle or make seem smaller.

entries.clue: Because of which, question crowds before bishop (7)

indicatorNotes.crowds: to crowd round something is to surround it

blocks.note: why? is a question; it crowds the rest

annotation.surface: People crowding round a bishop to ask him something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' reads as positional, putting one part ahead of another, but it is ERE, which stays ahead of B anyway.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a formal relative word, as in 'a rule whereby members pay', meaning by or because of which.

entries.clue: Bribe wife, literally tense with anticipation? (5)

annotation.surface: A husband bribing his nervous wife.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Literally' says to take the words at face value: wife gives W and 'on edge' gives EDGE. Wedge is British slang for a wad of money.
annotation.definitionFit: A wedge is slang for a sum of money, the kind handed over as a bribe.

entries.clue: Plant loaf intermittently on stove that doesn’t close (7)

indicatorNotes.that doesn’t close: a word that doesn't close loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A kitchen scene: bread baking in fits and starts on a stove with a faulty door.
annotation.walkthrough: A Primus is a portable paraffin camping stove, a trade name. 'Plant' reads as a verb, to put in the ground, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Primula is the genus of primroses and cowslips, a plant.

entries.clue: Finishing touch from Rada for new part on stage (5)

indicatorNotes.Finishing touch from: the finishing touch is the last letter

annotation.surface: A drama school graduate's last polish before a new part on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London. 'New part' reads as a role, but 'part on stage' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre term: the strip of stage that sticks out in front of the curtain, like an apron on a body.

entries.clue: 12 keeping horse in shape (7)

annotation.surface: Keeping a horse fit, like an entry number in a race card.
annotation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to 12 down, but it is just the time of day, noon.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a polygon with nine sides is one kind of shape.

entries.clue: Bird brought back flatfish, eating flounder’s tail in small quantities at a time (5,3,5)

annotation.definition: in small quantities at a time

indicatorNotes.brought back: letters brought back read in reverse
indicatorNotes.eating: a word eating a letter takes it inside
indicatorNotes.tail: a word's tail is its last letter

blocks.note: as printed; brought back to DRIB
sand dabs, small flatfish; they eat R

annotation.surface: A seabird returning with fish, pecking at a flounder's tail bit by bit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flatfish' is plural here: sand dabs. Flounder is itself a flatfish, which pulls the eye away from the dabs.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: drib and drab are old words for tiny amounts, so the pair means bit by bit.

entries.clue: Moved North Yorkshire market town wine stores (9)

indicatorNotes.stores: a word storing another holds it inside

blocks.note: Settle, a market town in North Yorkshire

annotation.surface: A Yorkshire wine shop, relocated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stores' reads as shops, but it is the verb: RED stores SETTLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Resettled means moved to a new home.

entries.clue: Scottish town’s half-hearted worry in review (5)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: half the heart is lost: one of the double letters in the middle goes
indicatorNotes.in review: reviewed means looked back over, read in reverse

blocks.note: a niggle is a small worry; NIGGLE loses one of its two middle Gs, then reads backwards

annotation.surface: A Scottish town with half-hearted concerns about a report.
annotation.walkthrough: The heart of NIGGLE is the GG pair in its middle, and half of it goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray, in the north-east of Scotland.

entries.clue: Spreading excessively, apparently many deliveries due (10)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is six balls, so overs are many deliveries

annotation.surface: An overworked postman with piles of parcels due.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' concedes the word is being split at an unnatural point. In cricket a delivery is one ball bowled, which the postal surface hides.
annotation.definitionFit: Oversowing is sowing seed too thickly, spreading it to excess.

entries.clue: Remnants of plot twisting, gentleman reflected (6)

indicatorNotes.twisting: twisting round turns the letters back

blocks.note: a bed = a garden plot; twisted to DEB
